identity.resolvedIdentity: The protected medieval stone church at Svanekilveien 11 on Kirkøy, identified by OSM way 543076065, Wikidata Q6493554, Kulturminne ID 84680 and Church of Norway building ID 444.
identity.identityProblem: The coordinate must identify the church building rather than the parsonage, cemetery, church office, Skjærhalden or a general Kirkøy or Hvaler locality point. Published sources also vary in the precise dating of the earliest stone church.
identity.splitReason: The medieval church building and immediate maritime church-site environment form one coherent place record. The parsonage, cemetery, Ørekroken and wider island landscape remain associated context.

requiredEvidence: heritage and Church of Norway identifiers
official building address and current institutional identity

evidence.finding: The mapped church-building polygon has representative point 59.03267, 11.02568 and identifies Hvaler church on Kirkøy.
evidence.reason: It directly represents the physical medieval church building rather than the wider island, parish or visitor infrastructure.

evidence.finding: The entity links Kulturminne ID 84680, Church of Norway building ID 444 and SSR 790650, and identifies the church at Svanekilveien 11 on Kirkøy.
evidence.reason: Confirms the building identity and registry relationships while the mapped polygon supplies the direct coordinate.

evidence.finding: The national heritage identifier is attached to Hvaler church as a protected medieval cultural property.
evidence.reason: Confirms the protected church identity without substituting legal protection geometry for the building point.

evidence.finding: The official church source identifies Hvaler church and the visitor address Svanekilveien 11, 1680 Skjærhalden.
evidence.reason: Confirms the current institutional and visitor identity.

evidence.finding: The municipal source describes the stone church as probably built around 1100 and as one of Norway's oldest stone churches.
evidence.reason: Supports the approximate year while preserving uncertainty rather than asserting one exact construction date.

evidence.finding: Norges Kirker identifies Hvaler as the main church of the islands and places the church east of the parsonage near Ørekroken, historically an important harbor during the herring fisheries.
evidence.reason: Defines the church-site and maritime context without replacing the building geometry as the coordinate source.

evidence.finding: The legacy coordinate lies approximately 644.3 metres northeast of the mapped church building.
evidence.reason: Replaced because it does not represent Hvaler church or its immediate church-site environment.

addressCandidates.rejectionReason: Confirms identity and access, while the church-building polygon is the more direct coordinate source.
